constipation and may require stool softeners. 
Medications Used to Treat Epilepsy 
Many of the anticonvulsant drugs (i.e., phenobarbital, carbamazepine) used to prevent seizures can also cause an 
increase in vitamin D metabolism in the liver and reduced bioavailability of vitamin D, which decreases calcium 
absorption in the intestine. This signals an increase in calcium uptake away from the bones. Low levels of vitamin D, 
serum calcium, and serum phosphate have been seen among children with epilepsy who receive these medications 
(Kija et al., 2019). 
Other nutritional deficiencies that can result from taking antiepileptic drugs include low levels of biotin, an increase 
in homocysteine levels, and a deficiency of several B vitamins (Samahan et al., 2020). Therefore, it is recommended 
that clients taking anticonvulsant medications take calcium and vitamin D supplements. It was also noted that high 
folate levels can increase homocysteine concentrations and, therefore, folate levels should be monitored (Safahani
